## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One critical defect needs fixing before merge: the new counting logic in `requirement_proven` returns `True` for an empty criteria list, which reverses the old result. The PR description says "No behavior change is intended", so this is a regression. This review read the full hunks for `h000_records.py`, `h001_records.py`, `h040_sorting.py` and `h091_requirements.py`, plus `tests/test_handlers.py`. It checked the other 178 record handlers by matching every added and removed diff line against the `h000` pattern: 2160 of 2167 added lines and 2340 of 2345 removed lines matched, and the rest belong to the special files. The `itemgetter("name")` change in `by_name` keeps the old ordering and still raises `KeyError` for a row without a name, as the lambda did.

## Changes
The PR replaces `typing.List`/`Dict` with built-in generics and `log.warn` with `log.warning` in 180 record handlers and `h091_requirements.py`. It also switches `by_name` to `operator.itemgetter`, rewrites `requirement_proven` to count proven criteria with `sum`, and adds a one-line root file `review.txt`.

## Critical
- app/handlers/h091_requirements.py:12 — correctness — Return False when criteria is empty — `requirement_proven([])` now returns `True`, but before this change it returned `False`. The old `return bool(criteria) and all(...)` short-circuited on an empty list. The new `proven = sum(...)` / `return proven == len(criteria)` compares `0 == 0`. The guard at lines 9–10 only logs "requirement has no criteria" and then falls through to that comparison. — A requirement with no criteria now counts as proven in release review, so a release can pass with no evidence at all. The PR description says no behavior change is intended. `tests/test_handlers.py:17-19` has no empty-list case, so the test suite will not catch this. — Fix: Return `False` inside the `if not criteria:` block after the warning, or restore `bool(criteria) and all(item["proven"] for item in criteria)`. Add `assert not requirement_proven([])` to `test_requirement_proof`.
